chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, he elevated it from al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
The Imam carries the recitations of those who follow behind him, except for the Opening Takbir.

key_terms.أَوْهَامَ: Plural of Wahm, referring to the recitations (Quranic chapters) of the followers
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَةَ اَلِافْتِتَاحِ: The Opening Takbir (saying 'Allahu Akbar' to begin the prayer)

ai.seo_question: Does the Imam carry the recitation of the congregation in prayer, and are there any exceptions?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the concept of 'carrying the doubts' (ahwam) of the followers highlights the Imam’s role in validating the prayer even if the congregation is uncertain about their recitation. This ruling underscores the theological principle of the Imam’s infallibility and authority in ritual practice, distinguishing the obligatory Takbirat al-Iftitah as a personal act of worship for each individual. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that the Imam’s recitation suffices for the followers in congregational prayers, reinforcing the hierarchical spiritual structure of the community.
